titulo: Unit 5: Modal Verbs & Future Passive (RA1, RA2, RA3)

paginas.contenido:
Unit 5 covers the use of modal verbs to express possibility, deduction, and necessity, as well as the passive voice for future actions.
  • RA1 & RA2: Reading technical specifications and possibilities.
  • RA3: Communicating ideas clearly in a professional environment.
  • Grammar Goals: Mastering Modals (may, must, could, should), Future Passive, and Adverbs of Manner.

💡 Nota: Los modales de deducción son vitales para formular hipótesis sobre el origen de un fallo técnico.

How to express how sure you are about something.
  • MAY / MIGHT: Possibility. "The system may fail if there is a power outage."
  • MUST HAVE: Strong deduction about the past. "The developer must have completed the update by now."
  • COULD HAVE: Past possibility that didn't happen. "They could have fixed the bug, but they didn't have time."
  • SHOULD HAVE: Past advice or expectation. "You should have backed up the data."

Used when the action is more important than the person doing it in the future.

Structure:

Subject + Will be + Past Participle

Examples:

  • "The system will be upgraded by the end of this week."
  • "New features will be implemented soon."
  • "The bugs will be fixed in the next patch."

💡 Nota: En IT, la pasiva se usa mucho para informes técnicos impersonales.

Adverbs describe how an action is performed.
  • Quickly: Rápido. "He will finish the report quickly."
  • Promptly: Con prontitud. "The team responds promptly to requests."
  • Efficiently: Eficientemente. "The application runs efficiently."

💡 Nota: Los adverbios suelen ir después del verbo o antes del verbo principal.

Comparing hardware or software performance.
  • Short Adjectives: Add -er. "Faster", "Slower".
  • Long Adjectives: Use more. "This smartphone is more expensive than the old one."

Key terms for the ongoing support of applications.
  • Bug: An error, flaw, or fault in a computer program.
  • Patch: A set of changes to a computer program to update, fix, or improve it.
  • Available: Able to be used or obtained.
  • Efficiency: The ability to avoid wasting materials, energy, efforts, money, and time.

Review these core concepts for Unit 5.
  • Modals: Use 'May' for possibility and 'Must have' for certainty.
  • Future Passive: Focus on the result ("Will be upgraded").
  • Adverbs: Describe how things are done ("Runs efficiently").
  • Comparatives: Compare systems using 'more' for long adjectives.
Complete this test to confirm you have mastered the Unit 5 content.

preguntas_test.q: The system __________ (upgrade) by the end of this week.
preguntas_test.explicacion: Voz pasiva en futuro (Will be + participio).

preguntas_test.q: The system __________ (fail) if there is a power outage.
The application __________ (run) efficiently on all devices.
preguntas_test.explicacion: Presente simple para un hecho general.
Estructura de futuro con adverbio de modo al final.

preguntas_test.q: The developer __________ (complete) the update by now.
preguntas_test.explicacion: Deducción lógica de que algo ha pasado = 'Must have' + participio.

preguntas_test.q: They __________ (fix) the bug, but they didn't have enough time.
preguntas_test.explicacion: Posibilidad pasada que no ocurrió = 'Could have' + participio.

preguntas_test.q: The team __________ (work) on the project since last month.
preguntas_test.explicacion: Presente perfecto para acción que sigue vigente (since).

preguntas_test.q: The IT team __________ (respond/promptly) to all requests.
preguntas_test.explicacion: El adverbio puede ir antes del verbo principal.

preguntas_test.q: This smartphone is ______ (expensive) than the one I bought last year.
preguntas_test.explicacion: Comparativo de superioridad para adjetivos largos = 'more' + adjetivo.
preguntas_test.ejemplo: Ej: 'This is more difficult than I thought.'
